clue.text: Drug hidden in crevice in beam

indicators.note: hidden in tells us the drug word is tucked inside the crevice word

parts.note: a slit is a narrow crevice or opening
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Narcotics stashed in a crack in a wooden beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like timber, but the definition is 'in beam', meaning lit by a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caught in a spotlight's ray is lit by that beam, so it is illuminated by it.

clue.text: Favourites raised the pace

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: pets are favourites, as in teacher's pets

explanation.surface: The favourites in a race picked up speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a single pace in walking.

clue.text: Leader of criminals to be imprisoned by soldiers for over four weeks

indicators.note: imprisoned by says the earlier pieces are locked inside the soldiers word

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of criminals

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang leader is held by troops for more than a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of' gives C, which with TO BE goes inside OR, 'imprisoned by'. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month has thirty-one days, a little longer than four weeks.

clue.text: Combination of drinks and drug is a mistake

parts.note: laps means drinks, as a cat laps milk
E is slang for ecstasy

explanation.surface: Mixing alcohol and drugs is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinks' looks like a noun but is the verb laps; 'Combination of' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or momentary failure is an error.

clue.text: Appreciating it's hard to get in all the petrol you need?

indicators.note: to get in says the letter for hard goes inside the fuel quantity

parts.note: a tankful fills the car completely
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A motorist finds it difficult to squeeze in a full load of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a link; H goes into TANKFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being grateful for something is to appreciate it.

clue.text: Catches sight of hot puddings?

definitions.meaning: spots or observes, as a verb
ices are cold desserts, so hot puddings are, whimsically

explanation.surface: Someone spots some warm desserts.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or observe something is to register it with the eyes; the second reading splits into NOT ICES.

clue.text: Citing meeting of North America and China?

parts.note: Ming porcelain is a famous kind of china, and Ming was a Chinese dynasty

explanation.surface: A summit between the USA and China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain: Ming vases. 'meeting of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mentioning or specifying something by name is quoting it.

clue.text: One has men on board ready for an opponent

definitions.text: One has men on board ready for an opponent

parts.words: One has men on board ready for an opponent
parts.note: reads like a chess or draughts board with pieces set up, but means a vessel carrying soldiers off to fight

explanation.surface: A chessboard set up with pieces for a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that carries soldiers to war has fighting men aboard to meet the enemy.

clue.text: Open with a play by Shaw

parts.note: candid means frank and open

explanation.surface: A theatre opens with a Shaw production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw wrote the 1894 comedy named after its heroine.

clue.text: Wear this out in the street, a casual garment

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: out signals the letters of wear this are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Advice to sport a relaxed top when out on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges WEAR THIS into WEATSHIR, placed 'in' ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose cotton jersey is informal clothing.

clue.text: Lots came swirling round head of psychic?

definitions.text: Lots came swirling round head of psychic?

indicators.note: round says the shuffled letters go around the other piece
swirling says the letters of lots came are churned into a new order
head of picks out the first letter of the word psychic

explanation.surface: Swirls of stuff appear around a medium's head at a séance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swirling' makes ECTOLASM from LOTS CAME, and 'round' puts P, the 'head of' psychic, inside it. The whole clue describes the substance said to flow from a medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists claimed a ghostly substance oozed from mediums in trance, a swirling exudation around them.

clue.text: Lightweight attack, short of power up front

indicators.note: short of says the attack word lacks the letter for power, and up front places it at the start

parts.note: to pounce is to attack suddenly
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A feeble assault lacking strength at its leading edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' with 'up front' removes P from the start of POUNCE. 'Lightweight' is a noun here: a small unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is one of the smallest imperial weights, a sixteenth of a pound.

clue.text: When material shatters in pot, possibly

parts.note: breaking is a synonym of shattering

indicators.note: possibly hints that the letters of in pot can be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Something smashes inside a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IN POT into POINT. The definition 'When material' reads with the rest: the moment at which material gives way.
explanation.definitionFit: The stress level at which a substance fails is its limit of endurance, the moment of fracture.

clue.text: Origins of some trendy residences newly erected getting urban acceptability

indicators.note: origins of takes the first letter of each of the next three words
newly signals the letters of erected made into something new

explanation.surface: Fashionable new homes bring a neighbourhood respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly' makes EETCRED from ERECTED; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means standing or credibility among fashionable city youth.

clue.text: Refuse to accept wrestling manoeuvre that's forbidden

parts.note: a throw floors an opponent in wrestling
out means not allowed, as in 'that's out'

explanation.surface: A referee rejects a banned wrestling hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject a proposal, such as a bill in parliament, is to dismiss it.

clue.text: They may be shown up in learned fields

parts.note: wise means learned or knowledgeable
acres are areas of land, fields

explanation.surface: Scholars exposed in their own academic disciplines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Know-alls who pretend to wisdom are prone to being exposed as frauds.

clue.text: Novel form of hat providing cover

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

indicators.note: form of says the letters of hat are put into another shape

explanation.surface: A new style of hat that gives protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective, but it names Haggard's adventure novel She; 'form of' makes ATH from HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting case for a blade is a protective covering.

clue.text: Complete eighteen holes

definitions.meaning: a full golf course: playing all of a round

explanation.surface: Finish a full round of golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete, versatile player is good at everything; eighteen holes make the whole golf round.

clue.text: Hens fluttering round me get caught in netting

indicators.note: round says the shuffled hens letters go around the next word
fluttering suggests the letters of hens flapping about into a new order

explanation.surface: Flapping chickens around the speaker become tangled in a net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' is the anagram signal and 'round' the container signal; the netted hens of the surface also suit the definition, which is a verb: to get something caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle something in a mesh is to trap it as in a net.

clue.text: Indistinctly pronounces a Welsh place name

definitions.meaning: speaks unclearly, as a verb in the third person
A headland and village near Swansea in Wales

explanation.surface: Someone mispronounces the name of a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mumbles is a seaside district by Swansea, South Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone muttering speaks unclearly; the Welsh district shares the word.

clue.text: Cunning article that's fatally attractive for insects

parts.note: fly is British slang for sharp or crafty
a paper is a written article or essay

explanation.surface: A clever trap that lures bugs to their death.
explanation.walkthrough: FLY as 'cunning' is British informal usage, as in 'a fly operator'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky strips hung up to trap flies lure insects that then die stuck to them.

clue.text: Seal future fate of Brit about to undertake operation again

indicators.note: about says the Brit word goes round the other piece

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person
to redo is to do again

explanation.surface: An Englishman is about to have surgery for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, not the usual RE; Pom is Australian and New Zealand slang for a Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn in advance is to fix someone's grim destiny beforehand.

clue.text: Ply part of the coast

definitions.meaning: a single thread or layer of yarn or rope

explanation.surface: Sailing along a stretch of shoreline.
explanation.definitionFit: A ply is one twist of a rope; the poetic word also means a shore.

clue.text: Forever giving consecutive jail sentences?

definitions.meaning: a judge stacking one prison term after another, a joke on doing time

explanation.surface: A judge hands down sentence after sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means repeatedly or on every occasion; 'time' is also slang for a prison term.

clue.text: Exhausted? Quite the reverse, when ' everything's taken into account

indicators.note: quite the reverse says the two words for exhausted swap places

parts.note: all in means tired out

explanation.surface: Tired? No, the opposite, once you count everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhausted' is ALL IN; 'Quite the reverse' swaps the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in total, altogether.

clue.text: It's a type of hill, some say (but only some)

indicators.note: but only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that something is a kind of hill, at least according to a few.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-topped elevation with steep sides is found in the American Southwest.

clue.text: Liner such as Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A great ocean liner, like the QE2.
explanation.walkthrough: The QE2 was a famous ocean liner, so the surface sets up a ship; instead 'Liner' is a tool for drawing lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring stick draws lines; a sovereign governs a realm.

clue.text: Superior tonsure?

parts.note: a monk's shaved crown is a haircut on top, read as a phrase meaning better than the rest

explanation.surface: A monk's shaved crown.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means noticeably better than others; a tonsure is literally a haircut on the head's top.

clue.text: Being no longer in service, rule of Captain Corcoran's broken?

definitions.meaning: in Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore the captain boasts he never uses a big, big D (swears); if that rule is broken

explanation.surface: A captain no longer serving breaks one of his own rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Corcoran in HMS Pinafore claims he 'hardly ever' swears 'a big, big D' (damn); breaking his rule means D IS USED.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment out of service is no longer employed, abandoned.

clue.text: I'd returned and left girl in a difficult situation

indicators.note: returned says the letters of I'd are read backwards

parts.note: the clue gives the letters I and D
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone came back and abandoned a girl in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns I'D into DI; 'in a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a hard choice between two unwelcome options.
